title: WIRED publishes essay titled ‘Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers’
dek: WIRED ran an essay called 'Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers' described as the author's final piece on the craft of coding.
body:
WIRED has published an essay titled "Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers." The one-line summary of the piece reads: "The last thing you should ever read,and the last thing I may ever write,about the craft of coding." Beyond that headline and tagline, the publicly available summary does not provide the essay's arguments, evidence, or author attribution.

## Why it matters
This is a prominent outlet framing the end of software programming as a subject worthy of a final essay. How WIRED positions coding matters because the magazine reaches technologists, managers, investors, and policymakers who pay attention to its cover stories and long-form commentary. That framing could shape conversations about skills, hiring, training, and technology coverage , but the specific claims and supporting evidence are not visible in the summary information at hand.

## The details
- Publication: WIRED published an essay carrying the title "Goodbye, World: The End of Programmers." 
- Tagline: The summary line is: "The last thing you should ever read,and the last thing I may ever write,about the craft of coding." 
- Content unknown: The summary provides no details about the essay's arguments, data, named people, products, dates, or policy recommendations. 
- Attribution unknown: The author of the essay is not identified in the available summary.
- Reactions unknown: There is no summary detail about industry, academic, or public response to the essay.

## What to watch
Read the full WIRED essay to see the claims, evidence, and who is making them. Watch for follow-up reporting that cites the essay and for responses from major developer communities, technology employers, and policy bodies — those reactions will reveal whether the piece shifts debate or is mainly rhetorical.

Source: reporting by WIRED.
